intervention_label: Trabectedin — mononuclear-phagocyte depletion
model_system: four syngeneic mouse tumour models plus human blood monocytes; myeloid-cell transfer and depletion experiments in trabectedin-resistant tumours
control_arm: vehicle-treated tumour-bearing mice; trabectedin-resistant tumour variants used to separate tumour-cell from myeloid effects
mechanism: Caspase-8 apoptosis triggered through TRAIL receptors. Monocytes carry signalling TRAIL receptors where neutrophils and lymphocytes carry decoys, which confines the killing to the mononuclear phagocyte compartment.
key_finding: Trabectedin killed monocytes and macrophages in blood, spleen and tumour while leaving other leukocytes intact, and tumour angiogenesis fell alongside them. Transfer and depletion experiments in trabectedin-resistant tumours placed the myeloid kill inside the antitumour effect rather than beside it. Monocyte counts, including tumour-associated macrophages, dropped in treated patients as well.
caveats: None of the four models is leiomyosarcoma, and the human confirmation is peripheral monocyte counts rather than sarcoma biopsies. Whether any of this reaches an infiltrative pulmonary metastasis is untested.

intervention_label: Trabectedin — macrophage differentiation and CCL2/IL-6 output
model_system: human blood monocytes, M-CSF-differentiated macrophages, and tumour-associated macrophages freshly isolated from ovarian cancer; monocyte counts in treated patients
control_arm: untreated monocytes/macrophages; lymphocytes as the comparator leukocyte population
dose_and_schedule: 5 nmol/L for cytotoxicity; sub-cytotoxic concentrations for differentiation and cytokine readouts
mechanism: DNA minor-groove binding with selective interference in inducible transcription; monocytes die at low nanomolar exposure, and below that concentration the drug shuts down CCL2 and IL-6 transcription.
key_finding: Monocytes underwent apoptosis at 5 nmol/L while lymphocytes tolerated roughly five-fold more drug. Sub-cytotoxic exposure blocked monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation and cut CCL2 and IL-6 output from monocytes, macrophages, ovarian TAMs and tumour cells alike.
caveats: Human cells in vitro plus ovarian TAMs; no sarcoma tissue anywhere in the paper. CCL2 suppression is the proposed link to reduced monocyte recruitment, inferred rather than measured in tumour.

intervention_label: Trabectedin — TC-NER- and VHL-dependent RNA Pol II degradation
model_system: isogenic repair-mutant human fibroblasts (CSB, XPA, XPC, XPD, XPF, XPG) and VHL-deficient cells, with complemented counterparts; several cancer cell lines
control_arm: repair-proficient parental lines and genetically complemented mutants; proteasome inhibition with MG132
mechanism: Trabectedin adducts recruit transcription-coupled nucleotide excision repair, and the stalled complex is resolved by proteasomal degradation of elongating RNA Pol II, which needs both TC-NER and an intact VHL complex.
key_finding: Transcribing RNA Pol II was degraded rapidly after trabectedin exposure, and cells defective in TC-NER or VHL failed to degrade it. VHL-deficient cells also resisted trabectedin killing, while XPC cells, defective only in global-genome repair, behaved like wild type.
caveats: Repair-mutant fibroblasts and epithelial lines, no sarcoma model. This is the reason trabectedin sensitivity tracks repair proficiency rather than proliferation rate, which is what separates it from a conventional cytotoxic.

intervention_label: ET-743 (trabectedin) + doxorubicin — preclinical basis for the combination
model_system: TE-671 rhabdomyosarcoma clonogenic assay and nude-mouse xenograft; C3H mice bearing UV2237M fibrosarcoma and its P-gp-overexpressing doxorubicin-resistant subline
control_arm: each drug alone and untreated controls; pharmacokinetic sampling in both single-agent and combination arms
dose_and_schedule: ET-743 1 h before doxorubicin, simultaneously, or 1 h after (three sequences compared)
mechanism: Two non-overlapping DNA-damage mechanisms — minor-groove alkylation whose cytotoxicity runs through transcription-coupled repair, versus topoisomerase II poisoning — combined without any pharmacokinetic interaction to account for the gain.
key_finding: Isobologram analysis gave combination indices just under 1, so the in-vitro interaction is additive at best. In vivo the pair produced log cell kill of 0.85-1.12 in TE-671 where either agent alone reached only 0.13-0.33, and the combination worked in a P-gp-positive subline resistant to both single drugs. Giving ET-743 one hour ahead edged out simultaneous or reversed dosing (LCK 1.12 vs 0.85 and 0.92), and doxorubicin levels in tumour, liver, heart and kidney were unchanged by co-administration.
caveats: Rhabdomyosarcoma and fibrosarcoma models from 2003; no leiomyosarcoma and no uterine model. The sequencing advantage rests on one small in-vivo comparison, and nothing in this or any other preclinical study addresses the trabectedin maintenance phase, which is an empirical clinical design.

intervention_label: Trabectedin before anti-PD-1 in a checkpoint-resistant model
model_system: murine fibrosarcoma poorly responsive to PD-1 blockade, in immunocompetent mice
control_arm: anti-PD-1 alone, trabectedin alone, and untreated tumours
dose_and_schedule: trabectedin given before anti-PD-1 (sequential, not concurrent)
mechanism: Removing tumour-associated macrophages lifts myeloid suppression; T-cell and interferon-response transcription rises, Pdcd1 goes up, and the tumour becomes answerable to PD-1 blockade.
key_finding: Treated tumours upregulated CD3, CD8, perforin, granzyme B and IFN-response genes, with a marked rise in Pdcd1. Trabectedin given ahead of anti-PD-1 improved efficacy in a model that otherwise resists checkpoint blockade.
caveats: Mouse fibrosarcoma, not LMS, and the benefit depended on trabectedin coming first. No preclinical data exist for adding checkpoint blockade to an LMS-04-style doxorubicin-trabectedin schedule.

exclusion_reason: Phase I/II clinical trial with paired on-treatment biopsies rather than a preclinical study. Logged because it is the human counterpart of the trabectedin macrophage literature: CD68+CD163+ macrophages fell in 9 of 28 biopsied sarcoma patients and the shift tracked with clinical benefit.
intervention_label: Metronomic trabectedin + low-dose cyclophosphamide (TARMIC)
Lurbinectedin — macrophage and monocyte depletion
model_system: tumour-bearing mice including a lurbinectedin-resistant tumour variant; purified human monocytes in vitro
control_arm: untreated tumour-bearing mice; resistant variant used to separate tumour-cell kill from microenvironment effects
mechanism: Same structural class as trabectedin: transcription and repair inhibition in tumour cells, plus caspase-8-dependent apoptosis of monocytes and suppression of CCL2, CXCL8 and VEGF at sub-lethal concentrations.
key_finding: Circulating monocytes, intratumoural macrophages and vessel density all fell, including in the resistant variant where the tumour cells themselves were untouched. Below the apoptotic dose, monocyte adhesion and migration collapsed alongside downregulation of Rho-GTPase family genes.
caveats: No sarcoma model and no doxorubicin combination, which is what the LMS trial (NCT06088290) actually tests. Accrual on that trial closed before this patient's diagnosis was corrected, so the row is mechanistic context.

intervention_label: Trabectedin + olaparib (PARP1-dependent synergy)
model_system: multiple sarcoma histotypes in vitro and subcutaneous plus orthotopic mouse xenografts, including the DMR leiomyosarcoma model and SJSA-1 osteosarcoma
control_arm: trabectedin alone, PARP inhibitor alone, vehicle; PARP1 overexpression and silencing as functional controls
mechanism: Trabectedin-induced single- and double-strand breaks activate PARP1; blocking PARP1 leaves that damage unresolved, driving G2/M arrest and apoptosis. The size of the effect scales with how much PARP1 the tumour expresses.
key_finding: Adding olaparib deepened DNA damage, G2/M arrest and apoptosis over trabectedin alone, with antitumour and antimetastatic activity in mice. Synergy was strong in the DMR leiomyosarcoma model and absent in SJSA-1 osteosarcoma, and it moved up or down when PARP1 was overexpressed or silenced.
caveats: The responsive LMS line is not uterine, and PARP1 expression, the proposed predictor, has never been measured in this patient. No clinical test of this combination in LMS exists.

intervention_label: Palbociclib in Rb-positive vs Rb-negative LMS cell lines
model_system: SK-LMS-1 (Rb-expressing) and SK-UT-1 (Rb-negative) leiomyosarcoma cell lines; genomic profiling of 18 LMS samples; p16/CDK4/CDK6/p-Rb IHC across 159 samples from 99 LMS patients
n_units: 18 tumour samples across 9 patients for profiling; 99 patients / 159 samples for IHC
control_arm: untreated cells; the Rb-negative line serves as the internal biological control
mechanism: Palbociclib blocks CDK4/6-mediated Rb phosphorylation. With no Rb protein present there is nothing downstream to hold, and the drug has no substrate through which to arrest the cycle.
key_finding: Palbociclib collapsed phospho-Rb (Ser780), slowed proliferation and forced G0/G1 arrest in Rb-positive SK-LMS-1, while Rb-negative SK-UT-1 was unaffected. CDK4 amplification turned up in 5 of 18 LMS samples, and an IHC-defined potential-responder phenotype in 29 of 99 patients.
caveats: Two cell lines, no in-vivo arm, and the responder phenotype is an IHC construct never tested prospectively. It is nonetheless the cleanest LMS-specific demonstration that one Rb stain sorts responders from non-responders.

intervention_label: RB loss as the determinant of CDK4/6-inhibitor failure
model_system: panel of breast cancer cell lines plus RB knockdown in immortalised mammary epithelium and multiple breast cancer subtypes; PD-0332991 (palbociclib)
control_arm: RB-proficient parental lines and non-targeting shRNA controls
mechanism: CDK4/6 inhibition works by keeping RB active as a transcriptional repressor of E2F targets and by holding down CDK2 activity. Chronic RB loss moves cells into a CDK4/6-independent state; acquired resistance follows the same logic through loss of CDK2 restraint.
key_finding: Chronic RB loss produced CDK4/6 independence and resistance to palbociclib, and direct RB knockdown reproduced it. Acquired resistance in initially sensitive models mapped to attenuated CDK2 inhibitors, so redundancy within the cell-cycle machinery is a second route to failure.
caveats: Breast models throughout. Carried here because it supplies the mechanistic reason an Rb-intact requirement is a real eligibility gate rather than an enrichment preference.

intervention_label: Palbociclib priming of Rb-positive sarcoma, including LMS PDX
model_system: SK-LMS1 leiomyosarcoma and HT-1080 fibrosarcoma lines; SK-LMS1 xenografts and Rb-positive patient-derived xenografts from leiomyosarcoma patients
control_arm: single-agent palbociclib, single-agent AZD1775, vehicle; concurrent versus sequential dosing compared
dose_and_schedule: palbociclib to arrest, then drug removal followed by doxorubicin or the Wee1 inhibitor AZD1775 (sequential scheduling)
mechanism: Palbociclib holds Rb-positive cells in a reversible G1 arrest; on release they move through the cycle within 6-24 hours, and a synchronised S-G2 population is more vulnerable to agents that act there.
key_finding: Palbociclib arrest was fully reversible, and priming Rb-positive sarcoma cells this way made them more sensitive to doxorubicin and to Wee1 inhibition. The palbociclib-AZD1775 synergy held in SK-LMS1 xenografts and in Rb-positive leiomyosarcoma PDX.
caveats: LMS PDX but no stated uterine primary. The sensitisation depends on sequencing — arrest, release, then the S-G2 agent — which is the opposite of concurrent dosing (see McClendon 2012).

intervention_label: CDK4/6 inhibition antagonising concurrent cytotoxic therapy
model_system: RB-proficient and RB-deficient triple-negative breast cancer cell lines treated with palbociclib plus doxorubicin
control_arm: doxorubicin alone; RB-deficient lines as the internal control for RB dependence
dose_and_schedule: CDK4/6 inhibitor and doxorubicin given together (concurrent exposure)
mechanism: Genotoxic cytotoxicity needs cells to cycle. An RB-mediated G1 arrest pulls them out of the phase where the damage is lethal, so the arrest shields the cell rather than adding to the kill.
key_finding: In RB-proficient models the pairing was cytostatically cooperative but protected cells from doxorubicin-mediated killing, and viable populations recurred after treatment. In RB-deficient cells palbociclib changed nothing about the doxorubicin response, confirming the protection runs through RB.
caveats: Breast models and doxorubicin rather than gemcitabine, but gemcitabine is likewise S-phase-dependent. This is the mechanistic caution to raise against a concurrent abemaciclib-plus-gemcitabine schedule in an Rb-intact tumour.

intervention_label: Selective CDK7 inhibition (YKL-5-124) in RB1/TP53-null tumours
model_system: human small-cell lung cancer lines and multiple aggressive murine SCLC models; SCLC is near-universally RB1- and TP53-null. YKL-5-124 given with and without anti-PD-1
control_arm: vehicle; anti-PD-1 alone; CDK7 inhibitor alone
mechanism: CDK7 sits at the junction of cell-cycle CDK activation and RNA Pol II transcription. Inhibiting it in cells that have already lost the RB1 restriction point disrupts cycle progression, forces replication stress and genome instability, and the resulting cytosolic DNA drives immune signalling.
key_finding: CDK7 inhibition blocked cycle progression and induced replication stress and genome instability while switching on immune-response signalling. The consequent T-cell surveillance was amplified by checkpoint blockade, and YKL-5-124 plus anti-PD-1 extended survival across several aggressive SCLC models.
caveats: SCLC is RB1-null like the trial's target population but is a different lineage entirely, and YKL-5-124 is not REC-617. No CDK7 data of any kind exist in leiomyosarcoma, which makes the RB1-null CDK7 door the thinnest mechanistic branch in this case.

exclusion_reason: Synovial sarcoma, where CDK7 dependency is argued from SS18-SSX-driven transcriptional addiction — a mechanism this tumour does not share. In vitro only (siRNA and BS-181), with no RB1 stratification.
intervention_label: CDK7 inhibition in synovial sarcoma

exclusion_reason: Pan-sarcoma expression-outlier analysis that lands on chordoma; leiomyosarcoma was not among the subtypes with CDK7 outlier overexpression, and the cell-line work is chordoma only. Reviewed as the closest thing to a sarcoma-wide CDK7 rationale, and it does not support one in LMS.
intervention_label: Pan-sarcoma CDK/cyclin outlier expression (CDK7 in chordoma)
ATRX loss and ALT in uterine leiomyosarcoma (target biology)
model_system: whole-exome sequencing of 19 uterine leiomyosarcomas; ATRX IHC in 44 uLMS; telomere-specific FISH for the ALT phenotype
n_units: n=19 exomes; n=44 tumours for IHC
control_arm: not applicable — descriptive human tumour series
mechanism: ATRX loads H3.3 at telomeric chromatin; losing it destabilises telomere maintenance and permits recombination-based lengthening, which is the ALT phenotype that ATR inhibition was proposed to exploit.
key_finding: TP53 was mutated in 6/19, ATRX in 5/19 (every alteration nonsense or frameshift) and MED12 in 4/19. ATRX expression was clearly reduced in 23 of 44 tumours by IHC, and every ATRX-low tumour tested ALT-positive by telomere FISH.
caveats: Descriptive human series with no therapeutic arm; the ATR-inhibitor suggestion in its discussion is an extrapolation from Flynn 2015, not a result. The tight ATRX-IHC-to-ALT concordance is what makes one stain a usable surrogate here.

intervention_label: LMS genomic landscape: TP53/RB1 loss, ALT, and BRCAness
model_system: whole-exome and transcriptome sequencing of leiomyosarcoma tumours plus short-term cultured LMS cells treated with olaparib or cisplatin
control_arm: untreated cultured LMS cells for the drug-sensitivity work
mechanism: Near-universal TP53 and RB1 inactivation with widespread copy-number change, chromothripsis and whole-genome duplication; telomere maintenance runs through ALT, and structural-rearrangement burden with the associated mutational signatures produces a BRCAness state that PARP inhibition can act on.
key_finding: TP53 and RB1 were inactivated in nearly every tumour, alternative telomere lengthening was present in 78% of cases, and recurrent alterations hit ATRX, RBL2 and SP100. Most tumours carried hallmarks of BRCAness, and cultured LMS cells were sensitive to olaparib and to cisplatin.
caveats: Mixed LMS sites rather than uterine-only, and the drug sensitivity is short-term culture with no in-vivo arm. The near-universal RB1 loss is the single most decision-relevant number here: it shifts the prior for an Rb IHC toward null and away from the abemaciclib door.

intervention_label: ATR inhibition in ALT-positive cells (original claim)
model_system: ALT-positive and telomerase-positive human cancer cell lines, including ATRX-manipulated pairs; ATR inhibitors in vitro
control_arm: telomerase-positive (non-ALT) cell lines
mechanism: ATRX loss uncouples cell-cycle control of the telomeric transcript TERRA, leaving RPA bound to telomeres after replication. That nucleoprotein structure is recombinogenic and depends on ATR, which RPA itself recruits.
key_finding: ATR inhibition disrupted the ALT process and caused chromosome fragmentation and apoptosis, with killing reported as selective for ALT-dependent cancer cells.
caveats: Cell lines only, no in-vivo arm, and the central selectivity claim was not reproduced by Deeg 2016 or by the osteosarcoma panel in Goncalves 2020. Treat as the hypothesis that opened the field rather than as a settled vulnerability.

intervention_label: ATR inhibition in ALT cells — failed replication
model_system: panel of ALT-positive and telomerase-positive human cell lines plus isogenic pairs in which ALT was active or suppressed; ATR inhibitor VE-821
control_arm: isogenic ALT-suppressed counterparts — the control Flynn 2015 lacked
mechanism: Same premise as Flynn 2015, tested with isogenic controls that hold genetic background constant while switching ALT on or off.
key_finding: No general ATR-inhibitor sensitivity followed from ALT status. Sensitivity differences tracked with line-to-line background rather than with the telomere maintenance mechanism.
caveats: Small line panel and a single ATR inhibitor, so it does not exclude a narrower ALT-related vulnerability. It does undercut any claim that ATRX loss alone predicts ATR-inhibitor benefit.

intervention_label: ATR inhibitors in sarcoma lines: telomere length, not ALT, tracked sensitivity
model_system: 17 osteosarcoma-derived cell lines characterised for telomere maintenance mechanism and telomere length; AZD-6738 (ceralasertib), VE-822 and BAY-1895344
control_arm: ALT-positive and telomerase-positive long-telomere lines compared against short-telomere lines
mechanism: ATR sustains chromosome stability when telomeres are critically short; the dependency follows telomere length rather than the mechanism used to maintain it.
key_finding: Short telomeres, not ALT, predicted hypersensitivity to all three ATR inhibitors, with chromosome bridges and cell death inside 24 hours. ALT-positive lines carried excessive telomere length and were no more sensitive than telomerase-positive controls.
caveats: Osteosarcoma rather than LMS, and in-vitro only. Within sarcoma this is the most directly damaging evidence against treating ALT positivity as an ATR-inhibitor biomarker, and it points to telomere length as the measurement that would actually matter.

intervention_label: PARP inhibition in HR-deficient uterine leiomyosarcoma (PDX)
model_system: patient-derived xenografts from HRD uterine leiomyosarcoma, including a paired PDX derived after PARP-inhibitor exposure; WGS/WES/panel screening of a 58-patient uLMS cohort
n_units: 58 patients screened; 5 (9%) HRD; PDX generated from HRD cases including one post-PARPi pair
control_arm: olaparib alone and olaparib plus cisplatin compared against the PARP1-selective AZD5305
mechanism: Homozygous BRCA2 deletion and COSMIC signature 3 with high genome-wide LOH define an HR-deficient subset; PARP inhibition converts unrepaired single-strand damage into lethal double-strand breaks, and PARP1-selective trapping does so with less of the off-target PARP2 burden.
key_finding: All 13 uLMS analysed by WGS carried a dominant signature 3, and 5 of 58 patients had HRD uLMS, in every confirmed case through homozygous BRCA2 deletion. PDX responses were fastest, deepest and most durable with the PARP1-selective AZD5305 rather than olaparib or olaparib plus cisplatin, holding even in a PDX derived after clinical PARPi exposure that had acquired PRKDC resistance mutations.
caveats: Small PDX numbers and a paper that interleaves patient outcomes with model pharmacology. The agent that worked best, AZD5305, is not the one this patient could reach; the accessible branch is olaparib plus temozolomide.

intervention_label: RAD51 nuclear-foci assay as a functional HRD readout
model_system: breast cancer patient-derived xenograft panels treated with olaparib, plus archival clinical tumour samples including PALB2-related cancers
control_arm: genomic HRD score and exome/BRCA1-methylation analysis run head-to-head against the RAD51 score
mechanism: RAD51 nuclear foci in replicating cells report whether homologous recombination is actually executing at the time of testing, which a sequencing panel cannot show — a gene may be intact and the pathway still broken, or mutated and functionally reverted.
key_finding: The RAD51 score separated PARPi-sensitive from PARPi-resistant PDX and outperformed the genomic HRD score in an independent panel. In archival samples the assay classified every PALB2-related tumour as HR-deficient, extending the deficient population beyond BRCA1/2 carriers.
caveats: Breast PDX and breast archival tissue; the assay needs proliferating cells and geminin co-staining, so specimen quality governs interpretability. Its only uLMS outcome data are the 22-patient NCI 10250 trial, where RAD51-defined HR deficiency separated PFS of 11.2 from 5.4 months.

intervention_label: PARP trapping as the reason olaparib pairs with temozolomide
model_system: genetically modified chicken DT40 lymphoma lines with human DU145 prostate and SF295 glioblastoma cells; olaparib and veliparib against temozolomide, camptothecin, cisplatin and etoposide
control_arm: veliparib, a potent catalytic inhibitor that traps poorly, as the mechanistic contrast to olaparib
mechanism: PARP inhibitors kill in two separable ways: catalytic blockade, and trapping of PARP-DNA complexes at damage sites. Which one matters depends on the partner drug — temozolomide-induced N-methylpurine lesions recruit PARP1 to base-excision intermediates, where a trapped complex becomes the lethal lesion.
key_finding: Temozolomide combinations needed trapping as well as catalytic inhibition, and olaparib, the stronger trapper, outperformed veliparib. Camptothecin combinations ran on catalytic inhibition alone, and cisplatin or etoposide gained little or nothing from either drug.
caveats: Avian and epithelial cell lines, no sarcoma and no in-vivo arm. Its value here is explaining why the uLMS trial regimen pairs olaparib with temozolomide specifically rather than with a platinum.

intervention_label: PARP inhibitor + temozolomide in sarcoma xenografts
model_system: Pediatric Preclinical Testing Program in-vitro panel and xenografts, including 10 Ewing sarcoma models; talazoparib with temozolomide or topotecan
n_units: 10 Ewing sarcoma xenograft models among a broader panel
control_arm: talazoparib alone, temozolomide alone, vehicle
dose_and_schedule: talazoparib 0.1 mg/kg BID × 5 d with temozolomide 30 mg/kg/d × 5 (combination A); or talazoparib 0.25 mg/kg BID × 5 d with temozolomide 12 mg/kg/d × 5 (combination B)
mechanism: Trapping-competent PARP inhibition converts temozolomide base damage into replication-blocking lesions; pharmacodynamic loss of PARP appeared only in models that responded.
key_finding: Talazoparib potentiated temozolomide up to 85-fold in vitro, with the largest shifts in Ewing sarcoma and leukaemia lines. In vivo the combination was significantly synergistic in 5 of 10 Ewing xenografts and only modestly active in most other models, and both schedules represented the maximum tolerated combination.
caveats: Ewing sarcoma, where PARPi sensitivity is driven by EWS-FLI1 rather than HR deficiency, so the mechanism is not the one proposed for uLMS. Talazoparib traps far more strongly than olaparib, making the potentiation an upper bound, and the myelosuppression that dominates the clinical regimen is exactly what the tolerability ceiling here predicts.

intervention_label: Sarcoma immune classes and B-cell-rich tertiary lymphoid structures
model_system: gene-expression profiling of 608 soft-tissue sarcoma tumours with in-situ validation in an independent cohort and a phase 2 pembrolizumab trial
control_arm: not applicable — classification study with a prospective response cohort attached
dose_and_schedule: pembrolizumab per the phase 2 trial protocol
mechanism: Response to PD-1 blockade in sarcoma tracks with the composition of the microenvironment rather than with tumour mutational burden. B-cell-rich tertiary lymphoid structures mark the class where antigen presentation is organised enough for checkpoint blockade to act on.
key_finding: Five microenvironment phenotypes emerged: two immune-low, two immune-high, one highly vascularised. B-cell content was the strongest prognostic factor even after accounting for CD8 T cells and cytotoxic signature, and the TLS-rich class E showed both better survival and a high response rate to pembrolizumab.
caveats: Leiomyosarcoma falls predominantly into the immune-low and highly vascularised classes, which is the structural reason checkpoint blockade underperforms in this histology. Response rates are reported by class, not by histology, so no LMS-specific number can be read off this paper.

intervention_label: Single-cell map of the metastatic uLMS microenvironment
model_system: single-cell RNA sequencing of four metastatic lesions (pelvic cavity, rectum, peritoneum, bladder) from one treatment-naive uterine leiomyosarcoma patient, against five normal myometrium samples; multiplex immunofluorescence validation and TCGA-SARC survival correlation
n_units: n=1 patient (4 metastatic sites); n=5 normal myometrium controls
control_arm: normal uterine myometrium
mechanism: An immunosuppressed niche built from exhausted CD8 T cells (LAG3, HAVCR2, TIGIT), M2-polarised CD163+ macrophages and immature N2 neutrophils, with MIF-CD74/CD44 and CXCL8 signalling sustaining angiogenesis and macrophage polarisation.
key_finding: The metastatic microenvironment was dominated by exhausted CD8 T cells and M2 macrophages rather than by any effector population, with naive markers (CCR7, MAL) lost along the pseudotime trajectory. The macrophage-heavy composition is the same compartment trabectedin depletes.
caveats: One patient. Descriptive, hypothesis-generating, and no therapy was given; it earns its place only because uLMS-specific microenvironment data at single-cell resolution are otherwise almost absent.

intervention_label: ATRA differentiating immature myeloid suppressor cells
model_system: multiple tumour-bearing mouse models with adoptive transfer of immature myeloid cells; ATRA combined with two cancer vaccines
control_arm: vaccine alone and untreated tumour-bearing mice
dose_and_schedule: ATRA administered in vivo to tumour-bearing mice (schedule per original protocol)
mechanism: ATRA drives immature myeloid cells to differentiate into dendritic cells, macrophages and granulocytes, which removes the suppressive population rather than killing tumour cells directly.
key_finding: ATRA sharply reduced immature myeloid cells across every model tested, and adoptive transfer confirmed the cells had differentiated rather than died. CD4 and CD8 tumour-specific responses improved and vaccine effects lasted longer, with no direct antitumour activity of ATRA itself.
caveats: Vaccine-era mouse models with no sarcoma and no checkpoint blockade; the trial pairs ATRA with cemiplimab, a combination this work predates. Doi not indexed in PubMed for this record, so the identifier is left null rather than guessed.

intervention_label: B7-H3 expression across soft-tissue sarcoma subtypes
model_system: immunohistochemistry on 153 soft-tissue sarcoma specimens spanning 15 subtypes, scored in tumour and in associated vasculature
control_arm: not applicable — expression survey; PD-L1 and PD-1 status compared where previously assessed
mechanism: B7-H3 (CD276) is a cell-surface immune-regulatory molecule with limited normal-tissue expression, which is what makes it usable as an ADC or CAR target rather than as a driver.
key_finding: B7-H3 was expressed in 97% of specimens and at high level in 69.2%, with vascular positivity in 94.7%. Expression was independent of prior treatment, tumour size, grade and patient age, and uncorrelated with PD-L1 or PD-1.
caveats: Prevalence only — no functional or therapeutic readout, and per-subtype numbers for leiomyosarcoma are not broken out in the abstract. High prior probability of a positive stain is not the same as a dependency, and vascular positivity raises a separate on-target question.

intervention_label: B7-H3 CAR T cells and the antigen-density threshold
model_system: xenograft models of osteosarcoma, medulloblastoma and Ewing sarcoma; B7-H3 CAR T cells tested against targets differing in surface antigen density
control_arm: control T cells without the B7-H3 CAR; target cells expressing low versus high surface B7-H3
mechanism: CAR T-cell killing scales with the number of antigen molecules per target cell. Below a threshold density the synapse fails to trigger, which is what creates a therapeutic window despite low-level B7-H3 on normal tissue.
key_finding: B7-H3 CAR T cells caused regression of established solid tumours across several xenograft models. Efficacy depended heavily on surface antigen density and fell away sharply against low-expressing targets.
caveats: Pediatric solid-tumour xenografts, no leiomyosarcoma model and no ADC. The density dependence is the transferable point: it is why an IHC-positive result alone does not establish that a B7-H3 agent will work, and why the 69% 'high' stratum matters more than the 97% positivity figure.

intervention_label: Vobramitamab duocarmazine (MGC018) with bystander killing
model_system: human neuroblastoma cell lines, multicellular tumour spheroids, and orthotopic, pseudometastatic and resected mouse neuroblastoma models; co-culture of B7-H3-negative murine NX-S2 cells with B7-H3-positive human cells
control_arm: irrelevant (anti-CD20) duocarmycin ADC; topotecan-temozolomide as the standard-of-care comparator
dose_and_schedule: 1 mg/kg IV weekly × 3 weeks, extended to 4 weeks and repeated cycles in survival experiments
mechanism: A cleavable valine-citrulline linker releases membrane-permeable duocarmycin, so payload liberated inside an antigen-positive cell can cross into neighbouring antigen-negative cells — the bystander effect that makes heterogeneous or low antigen tractable.
key_finding: Cytotoxicity ran from IC50 5.1-53.9 ng/mL in monolayer and 17.8-364 ng/mL in spheroids. B7-H3-negative murine cells, untouched by the ADC alone, were killed when co-cultured with B7-H3-positive cells, and treatment delayed or arrested relapse across orthotopic and resected models without weight loss or haematologic toxicity.
caveats: Neuroblastoma throughout, with no sarcoma model and no leiomyosarcoma. The bystander demonstration is the part that transfers, and it is the mechanistic argument for a B7-H3 ADC where expression is heterogeneous rather than uniform.

intervention_label: FAP-2286 radioligand — preclinical imaging and therapy
journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging
model_system: FAP-expressing HEK293 tumours and sarcoma patient-derived xenografts in mice; IHC and autoradiography on primary human cancer specimens including sarcoma
control_arm: FAPI-46, a small-molecule FAP agent, as the head-to-head comparator; non-FAP-expressing tumours for specificity
mechanism: A cyclic peptide binder coupled to a chelator: it holds at FAP-positive tissue long enough for a bound beta emitter to deposit dose, with renal clearance keeping normal-tissue exposure low.
key_finding: Tumour uptake was rapid and persistent across all three radionuclides with minimal normal-tissue signal, and 177Lu-FAP-2286 produced antitumour activity in FAP-expressing HEK293 tumours and in sarcoma PDX without significant weight loss. Tumour retention and suppression outlasted FAPI-46.
caveats: The sarcoma evidence is PDX efficacy without histology-level detail, and PDX stroma is host mouse tissue, so what the ligand engaged in those tumours is not resolvable from the report. The engineered HEK293 model tests direct antigen binding rather than the stromal-crossfire premise.

intervention_label: FAP expression in sarcoma: stroma and tumour cells
model_system: IHC on 63 bone and soft-tissue tumour samples with 30 adjacent normal tissues, scored separately for stromal and tumour-cell compartments; RNA-seq comparison across 10,626 samples and survival analysis in 168 sarcomas
n_units: n=63 tumours; n=30 adjacent normal; n=168 sarcomas for survival
control_arm: adjacent normal tissue and positive controls
mechanism: FAP is a marker of activated fibroblasts. In mesenchymal tumours the malignant cell is itself of fibroblastic lineage, so the antigen is not confined to the stromal compartment the way it is in carcinomas.
key_finding: Intensity ≥2 with density ≥25% appeared in stromal cells of 77.7% of tumours and in tumour cells of 50.7%. Sarcomas ranked among the highest FAP-expressing cancer types by RNA-seq, and FAP level carried no overall-survival association.
caveats: Mixed bone and soft-tissue histologies with no leiomyosarcoma breakout, and no functional or therapeutic arm. It does change the mechanistic argument: in sarcoma a FAP radioligand may deliver dose directly to tumour cells rather than relying solely on crossfire from stroma.

intervention_label: On-target toxicity of FAP-directed therapy
model_system: FAP-reactive CAR T cells transferred into mice bearing a variety of subcutaneous tumours, across two mouse strains; FAP staining of 18 human tumours and of mouse and clinical-grade human multipotent bone marrow stromal cells
n_units: 18 human tumours stained; two mouse strains tested
control_arm: untreated and control-CAR tumour-bearing mice
mechanism: FAP is not tumour-restricted. It is expressed on PDGFR-α+ Sca-1+ multipotent bone marrow stromal cells in mice and on clinical-grade human BMSCs, so any FAP-directed effector reaches the marrow niche.
key_finding: FAP-reactive CAR T cells were only weakly active against tumours yet caused significant cachexia and lethal bone toxicity in two mouse strains. Both mouse and human multipotent BMSCs were recognised by the same T cells.
caveats: A CAR T-cell platform rather than a radioligand, and the dose delivered to marrow stroma by a peptide with renal clearance is not the same exposure. It remains the sharpest evidence that FAP positivity on a PET scan does not make FAP a tumour-exclusive target.

intervention_label: Alpha versus beta FAP-targeted radionuclide therapy
journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging
model_system: human-FAP-expressing lung tumour model in immunocompetent mice; FAP-targeting single-domain antibody 4AH29 labelled with 225Ac or 131I, with and without PD-L1 blockade
control_arm: vehicle solution; PD-L1 blockade alone
dose_and_schedule: [131I]I-GMIB-4AH29 and [225Ac]Ac-DOTA-4AH29 at low and high doses; high-dose 225Ac combined with PD-L1 checkpoint blockade
mechanism: Alpha emission deposits high linear-energy-transfer dose over a few cell diameters while a beta emitter spreads a lower dose further; the report also links radionuclide therapy to PD-L1 upregulation, which supplies the rationale for adding checkpoint blockade.
key_finding: Tumour uptake was high for both radionuclides, with 225Ac retention decaying far more slowly (2.1 to 1.7 %IA/g between 1 and 24 h) than 131I (3.5 to 0.9 %IA/g). Both improved survival over vehicle, PD-L1 rose in 225Ac-treated tumours, and the 225Ac-plus-PD-L1-blockade combination was synergistic.
caveats: FAP was engineered onto the tumour cells, so this tests direct antigen targeting rather than the stromal-to-tumour crossfire that FAP therapy in a sarcoma would depend on. Lung carcinoma model, different binder chemistry from either agent this patient could reach.

intervention_label: Intratumoural hypoxia, HIF-1α/PLOD2 and sarcoma lung metastasis
model_system: autochthonous LSL-KrasG12D/+; Trp53fl/fl murine undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma and allografts, with HIF-1α or PLOD2 deletion and PLOD2 rescue; human sarcoma expression analysis
control_arm: HIF-1α-proficient and PLOD2-proficient tumours; ectopic PLOD2 re-expression in HIF-1α-deficient tumours
mechanism: Hypoxia drives HIF-1α to induce PLOD2, which modifies and organises collagen in the primary tumour. That altered matrix supports migration and dissemination without affecting primary tumour growth.
key_finding: Losing HIF-1α or PLOD2 disrupted collagen modification, cell migration and pulmonary metastasis while leaving primary growth intact, and re-expressing PLOD2 restored metastatic potential in HIF-1α-deficient tumours. Human metastatic primary lesions carried elevated HIF1A and PLOD2, and pharmacologic PLOD inhibition suppressed metastases.
caveats: This is intratumoural hypoxia in a UPS model and speaks to lung tropism in sarcoma generally. It says nothing about ambient hypoxia at 2,600 m: no sarcoma model has been run under chronic hypobaric conditions, and the two forms of hypoxia are not interchangeable.

intervention_label: Hypoxic preconditioning and doxorubicin cardiomyopathy
model_system: Wistar rats given doxorubicin, with or without intermittent hypoxic preconditioning beforehand; no tumour present
control_arm: doxorubicin without preconditioning; untreated rats
dose_and_schedule: doxorubicin 4 mg/kg IP weekly × 4; intermittent hypoxic preconditioning for 2 weeks before the first dose
mechanism: Preconditioning raised SERCA2a expression, which the authors link to preserved calcium handling; HIF-1α levels did not change, and TRPV1/TRPV4 loss and suppressed CaMKII activation followed doxorubicin regardless.
key_finding: Preconditioned rats retained more cardiac output than rats given doxorubicin alone, with higher SERCA2a on western blot and no change in HIF-1α.
caveats: Cycled normobaric hypoxia in healthy rats is not continuous residence at 8,500 ft, no tumour was present, and the mechanism is inferred from protein levels rather than measured function. Logged to record that the altitude question has no translatable preclinical answer — direction of effect is unresolved and should not be used either to reassure or to alarm.

intervention_label: LOXO-101 (larotrectinib) against an LMNA-NTRK1 fusion
model_system: TRK-fusion-bearing human cancer cell lines in vitro and in vivo, alongside a soft-tissue sarcoma patient with lung metastases carrying an LMNA-NTRK1 fusion confirmed by in-situ proximity ligation
n_units: n=1 patient; cell-line panel size not stated
control_arm: non-fusion cell lines for selectivity
mechanism: Selective ATP-competitive inhibition of TRKA/B/C. A fusion partner drives constitutive kinase activation, making the whole tumour dependent on that one signal, which is why response is fast when the fusion is genuinely the driver.
key_finding: Fusion-bearing cell lines showed inhibition of the fusion oncoprotein with reduced proliferation in vitro and tumour growth in vivo. The sarcoma patient had rapid, substantial tumour regression with improvement in dyspnea and oxygen saturation.
caveats: Preclinical content is thin next to the clinical case, and NTRK fusions are rare in leiomyosarcoma. Carried because the fusion has never been tested here and spindle-cell morphology with an earlier benign sign-out is the setting where an NTRK-rearranged mesenchymal tumour is missed.
